reason: Never became controllable within a generous probe budget under two independent probe designs. capture_start_state.py's generic mash schedule (START/START/A/START pulses, 6-on/10-off cadence) ran to 2400 frames then re-ran to 6000 frames (100 emulated seconds) -- both attempts returned 'never became controllable', no candidate state written. A second, independent probe (raw NOOP hold, no scripted mashing) advanced 3600 frames (60 emulated seconds) sampling cpu_state()/ppu_state()/peek_nametables()/rendered frames every 60-900 frames: the physical nametable VRAM stayed 0/2048 nonzero bytes at every single sample point (visually confirmed via 11 rendered frames, all pure black, runs/onboard_wave5/probe_seq_*.png), 2KB CPU RAM stayed pinned at 155-156/2048 nonzero bytes the entire time (no meaningful state change), and the CPU program counter never left a ~32-byte address window (0xC8E0-0xC900) across the full 60 seconds -- the signature of a boot-time spin loop (most likely a wait-for-PPU-status/IRQ poll) that never resolves, not a slow logo fade or an unskippable-but-eventually-live cutscene.

asm_cpu_anomaly_cross_check.why: task brief flagged the possibility this mapper hits the same ASM-CPU NMI/PPU-batching flat-trace anomaly documented for Journey to Silius in docs/research/LEAGUE_ONBOARDING_WAVE4_2026-08-25.md -- checked directly before calling this a game-side mint failure.
asm_cpu_anomaly_cross_check.method: constructed nes_core.Pool(num_workers=1) twice, explicitly calling pool.set_disable_asm_cpu(True) (true interpreter, no ASM 6502 core) vs leaving the field at its Rust default False (ASM CPU on, matches Pool's live default per pool.rs / nes.rs:269) -- NOT just calling nes_core.NESEnvironment bare, because direct code inspection (nes_core/src/python.rs) showed NESEnvironment exposes no set_disable_asm_cpu at all and constructs Nes::new() with the same disable_asm_cpu:false default as Pool, so it is NOT a true interpreter-only cross-check by itself in the currently-installed build (Makefile's `make build` compiles the asm_cpu feature in unconditionally) -- only Pool's explicit setter can force interpreter-only execution.
asm_cpu_anomaly_cross_check.verdict: IDENTICAL stuck state in both ASM-CPU-on and true-interpreter modes -- rules out the ASM-CPU NMI-batching anomaly as the explanation. This is a genuine, instrument-independent boot hang, not a repeat of the Journey to Silius instrument bug. Not tagged possible-asm-cpu-anomaly.
